non_blocking_notes: Evidence-first pattern correctly implemented with pending keys preventing reentrant mutations
Deterministic discovery sorting ensures repeatable behavior across catalog queries
Strict mode gracefully downgrades to legacy behavior when require_catalog=False
Per-tenant capacity monotonic — entries only increase, preventing unbounded growth
All MCP access points validated: no credential leakage, no shell/filesystem/deployment access
result.reasoning_summary: FW-MCP-04 tenant-bound catalog implementation is deterministic, narrow, and evidence-first. The patch correctly binds tenant/tool/capability tuples with trust and enabled-state enforcement. Admission checks validate catalog state before allowing tool invocation. Thread safety is maintained via RLock on all catalog mutations. Reentrant safety is enforced through pending-keys tracking during Evidence-first registration. Per-tenant capacity limits prevent unbounded growth. Legacy mode (require_catalog=False) remains fully compatible. All 84 tests pass, covering registration, discovery, validation, capacity, reentrancy, and backward compatibility. No tool connections, credentials, shell access, or deployment authority present. Patch is focused and does not introduce scope creep or unrelated refactoring.
